lessons.title: -tion → -zione · Nouns of action / result
lessons.objective: Swap -tion for -zione and stress the -zio- syllable. The single most productive rule between English and Italian: information → informazione.
lessons.explanation: Nearly every -tion word works, and every one is feminine: l'informazione, la nazione. The one to watch is question: questione means an issue or matter; a question you ask is una domanda.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the -zio- syllable: in-for-ma-ZIO-ne; z sounds like ts. Plural le informazioni.
Stress the -zio- syllable: na-ZIO-ne, with z like ts. Feminine, plural le nazioni.
Stress con-ver-sa-ZIO-ne; z sounds like ts. Feminine, plural le conversazioni.

lessons.title: -sion → -sione · Nouns in -sion / -ssion
lessons.objective: -sion becomes -sione, and the noun is feminine: la decisione. The double s of -ssion stays double: passion → passione, discussion → discussione.
lessons.explanation: permission → permesso is the common slip: permissione does not exist.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress de-ci-SIO-ne. The c before i is soft, like ch in church; the s sounds like z.
Stress te-le-vi-SIO-ne. In everyday speech Italians often say la TV or la tivù.
Stress ver-SIO-ne. It can also mean a school translation exercise.

lessons.title: -ity → -ità · Abstract-quality nouns
lessons.objective: -ity becomes -ità, with a written accent on the final à. The noun is feminine: l'università, la comunità.
lessons.explanation: The plural does not change: le università, le qualità. In everyday speech, capacità is often used for ability.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: The written à carries the stress: a-bi-li-TA. Same form in the plural: le abilità.
Say qua- as kwa: qua-li-TA. The final à is stressed, and the plural is the same: le qualità.
The written à carries the stress: u-ni-ver-si-TA. Same form in the plural: le università.

lessons.title: -ty → -tà · Other -ty nouns
lessons.objective: Words that end in -ty usually become -tà: society → società, liberty → libertà. (Words in -ity follow the rule above.)
lessons.explanation: The letters before -tà often change (property → proprietà, majesty → maestà), so learn each one once.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the final à: li-ber-TA. The plural is the same: le libertà.
Also means company in business: una società di consulenza. Stress so-cie-TA; cie sounds like che in check, with no separate i.
Stress the final à: ma-e-STA. The letters before -tà change from English (majesty), so learn it as a whole word.

lessons.title: -ly → -mente · Adverbs
lessons.objective: Add -mente to the feminine form of the adjective: rapida → rapidamente. Thousands of adverbs for free.
lessons.explanation: Adjectives ending in -le or -re drop the final -e first: facile → facilmente, finale → finalmente, regolare → regolarmente.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Take the adjective probabile, drop the -e, add -mente: pro-ba-bil-MEN-te. Say the l and the m one after the other, with no vowel between.
The adjective reale drops its -e: re-al-MEN-te, four syllables. Everyday Italian often says davvero for really.
From finale, dropping the -e: fi-nal-MEN-te. It often expresses relief, like at last.

lessons.title: -ble → -bile · Adjectives in -ble
lessons.objective: -ible and -able become -ibile and -abile: possible → possibile, flexible → flessibile.
lessons.explanation: Double letters stay double, and the stress falls on the syllable before -bile: pos-SI-bi-le. comfortable is the exception: say comodo.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the double s and stress the syllable before -bile: pos-SI-bi-le.
Hold the double s: im-pos-SI-bi-le. Same form for masculine and feminine.
Hold the double r and stress ter-RI-bi-le. The plural is terribili.

lessons.title: -ist → -ista · People and -ist words
lessons.objective: Add -a: artist → artista. The singular is the same for men and women: il turista, la turista.
lessons.explanation: The plural shows the gender: i turisti for men or a mixed group, le turiste for women.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: One singular for men and women: l'artista. Plural gli artisti for men or a mixed group, le artiste for women.
Stress tu-RI-sta. Plural i turisti for men or a mixed group, le turiste for women.
Stress den-TI-sta. Plural i dentisti or le dentiste.

lessons.title: -ism → -ismo · Ideas and movements
lessons.objective: Add -o: tourism → turismo. Masculine nouns: il turismo, l'ottimismo.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each Italian word and its spelling: optimism → ottimismo, racism → razzismo.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress tu-RI-smo; the s before m sounds like z. Masculine: il turismo di massa means mass tourism.
Hold the double t: ot-ti-MI-smo. English pt becomes tt in Italian.
Stress re-a-LI-smo. Masculine, and the adjective is realistico.

lessons.title: -ic → -ico · Adjectives in -ic
lessons.objective: -ic becomes -ico. The stress falls on the third syllable from the end, with no written accent: elettrico, fantastico, pubblico.
lessons.explanation: Nouns often end in -ica instead: music → musica, politics → politica. In the plural, -ico usually becomes -ici: elettrici, classici.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress falls third from the end with no written accent: e-LET-tri-co. Hold the tt; plural elettrici, with a soft c.
Stress CLAS-si-co. Hold the double s; feminine classica, plural classici.
Stress MA-gi-co, with a soft g like j in jam. Feminine magica; the plural magici has a soft c, like ch in church.

lessons.title: -ical → -ico · Adjectives in -ical
lessons.objective: -ical becomes -ico: practical → pratico, political → politico.
lessons.explanation: A few keep -ale: musicale, tropicale, verticale. medico is also the everyday word for a doctor: il medico.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress ME-di-co. As a noun, il medico is the doctor; as an adjective it means medical.
Stress PRA-ti-co. It also describes a person who is handy and efficient.
Stress po-LI-ti-co. As a noun, il politico is the politician.

lessons.title: -al → -ale · Adjectives in -al
lessons.objective: Add -e: normal → normale, final → finale, hospital → ospedale. Italian adds nothing in front of s + consonant: special → speciale.
lessons.explanation: attuale means current, not actual; actually is in realtà.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Italian adds an -e: nor-MA-le. Same form for masculine and feminine; the plural is normali.
Stress a-ni-MA-le. Masculine, plural gli animali.
Stress fi-NA-le. As a noun, la finale is a sports final and il finale is the ending of a story.

lessons.title: -ive → -ivo · Adjectives in -ive
lessons.objective: -ive becomes -ivo: active → attivo. Change the final vowel with the gender (attiva).
lessons.explanation: Watch the spelling: ct becomes tt (active → attivo). effettivo means actual or real; effective is efficace.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress at-TI-vo, with a double t. Feminine attiva, plural attivi.
Stress cre-a-TI-vo. Feminine creativa, plural creativi.
Stress po-si-TI-vo. The s between vowels sounds like z; feminine positiva.

lessons.title: -ous → -oso · Adjectives in -ous
lessons.objective: -ous becomes -oso: famous → famoso. Feminine is -osa.
lessons.explanation: A few change completely: serious → serio, various → vari, dangerous → pericoloso.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress fa-MO-so. Feminine famosa, plural famosi; molto famoso means very famous.
Stress cu-RIO-so. It can mean curious (nosy) or strange and interesting.
Stress de-li-ZIO-so. The zio sounds like tsyo. Feminine deliziosa.

lessons.title: -ant / -ent → -ante / -ente · Adjectives and people in -ant / -ent
lessons.objective: Add -e: important → importante, different → differente. Many also name people: lo studente, il presidente.
lessons.explanation: Double letters stay: different → differente. In everyday speech, diverso is the more common word for different.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress im-por-TAN-te. Same form for masculine and feminine; the plural is importanti.
Hold the double f: dif-fe-REN-te. The plural is differenti.
Lo before st-: lo studente, plural gli studenti. Feminine is la studentessa.

lessons.title: -ence → -enza · Nouns in -ence
lessons.objective: -ence becomes -enza, and the noun is feminine: la scienza, l'esperienza.
lessons.explanation: udienza is a hearing, but a crowd at a show is il pubblico. conferenza is a lecture or talk; a big meeting is un congresso.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the ff: dif-fe-REN-za. The z sounds like ts; plural le differenze.
Stress the -RIEN- syllable: e-spe-RIEN-za. Spelled with s, not x; plural le esperienze.
Stress the -ZIEN- syllable: pa-ZIEN-za, with ts. Avere pazienza means to be patient.

lessons.title: -ance → -anza · Nouns in -ance
lessons.objective: -ance becomes -anza, feminine: l'importanza, la distanza.
lessons.explanation: A few -ance words take -enza instead: assistance → assistenza, resistance → resistenza.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the -tan- syllable: im-por-TAN-za. The z sounds like ts. It is rarely used in the plural.
Stress the middle syllable: di-STAN-za, with ts for the z. Plural le distanze; a long distance is una lunga distanza.
Stress the -lan- syllable: am-bu-LAN-za, not on the first syllable as in English. The z is ts; plural le ambulanze.

lessons.title: -ary → -ario · Nouns and adjectives in -ary
lessons.objective: -ary becomes -ario: necessary → necessario, dictionary → dizionario.
lessons.explanation: library is a false friend: biblioteca. A libreria is a bookshop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the double s: ne-ces-SA-rio, with ce as in chair. Feminine necessaria; the plural is necessari.
Stress the -na- syllable: or-di-NA-rio. It can also mean a full university professor, un professore ordinario.
Say o, not u, in the middle: vo-ca-bo-LA-rio. It also means a dictionary, in addition to a person's stock of words.

lessons.title: -ize → -izzare · Verbs in -ize
lessons.objective: -ize becomes -izzare, with a double z: organize → organizzare. They conjugate like any -are verb.
lessons.explanation: realizzare means to carry out or achieve. To realize (understand) is rendersi conto.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: The double zz is a long dz sound: or-ga-niz-ZA-re. Conjugates like parlare: organizzo, organizzi.
Warning: it means to achieve or make real, not to understand. Say re-a-liz-ZA-re with a long zz; to realize is rendersi conto.
This verb is reflexive: mi specializzo, ti specializzi. Hold the zz and stress -ZAR-: spe-cia-liz-ZAR-si, where cia sounds like cha.

lessons.title: -ate → -are · Verbs in -ate
lessons.objective: Replace -ate with -are: celebrate → celebrare, separate → separare.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each Italian word and its spelling: calculate → calcolare.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the -BRA- syllable: ce-le-BRA-re, with ce as in chair. It sounds formal; to party or mark an occasion, festeggiare is more common.
Stress the -RA- syllable: se-pa-RA-re. This is the verb only; the adjective separate is separato.
Note the o: cal-co-LA-re, not calcul-. The c is hard before a and o. A calculator is la calcolatrice.

lessons.title: -ify → -ificare · Verbs in -ify
lessons.objective: -ify becomes -ificare: identify → identificare.
lessons.explanation: clarify is the one to watch: Italians say chiarire.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: The c is hard before a: i-den-ti-fi-CA-re. It conjugates like parlare, adding h before i: identifico, identifichi.
Not simpli-: the first vowel is e, sem-pli-fi-CA-re, from semplice (simple). The c is hard before a.
Stress the -CA- syllable: ve-ri-fi-CA-re. The c is hard, so the present is verifico, verifichi, with ch before i.

lessons.title: -ct → -tto · Words in -ct
lessons.objective: ct becomes tt and the word adds -o: direct → diretto, perfect → perfetto.
lessons.explanation: The same change runs through fact → fatto, project → progetto, object → oggetto and subject → soggetto. A school subject is la materia.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the tt: di-RET-to. The feminine is diretta; a direct train is un treno diretto.
Hold the tt and stress the middle: per-FET-to. Feminine perfetta, plural perfetti.
Hold the tt: cor-RET-to, with the rr also long. It is also the word for a coffee with a drop of liquor, un caffè corretto.

lessons.title: -ology → -logia · Fields of study
lessons.objective: -ology becomes -logia, with the stress on the i: biology → biologia.
lessons.explanation: The noun is feminine and has no written accent: la biologia, la psicologia. Say bi-o-lo-GI-a.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the i: bi-o-lo-GI-a, with a soft g as in gelato. The word is feminine.
Stress the i: tec-no-lo-GI-a, with a soft g. The plural is le tecnologie.
Say the p: psi-co-lo-GI-a. The g is soft, and the plural is le psicologie.

lessons.title: -ologist → -ologo · Specialists in a field
lessons.objective: -ologist becomes -ologo (feminine -ologa): biologist → biologo.
lessons.explanation: The stress falls on the third syllable from the end: bi-O-lo-go. The plural is -ologi: i biologi, gli psicologi.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second syllable: bi-O-lo-go, with a hard g. Plural i biologi, with a soft g; feminine la biologa.
Say the p: psi-CO-lo-go. Lo before ps-, and the plural is gli psicologi.
Stress ge-O-lo-go: the first g is soft, the second hard. Plural i geologi; feminine la geologa.

lessons.title: -graphy → -grafia · Writing and recording words
lessons.objective: -graphy becomes -grafia, with the stress on the i: photography → fotografia.
lessons.explanation: ph becomes f and the noun is feminine: la geografia. In speech, la foto is the short form of la fotografia.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the i: ge-o-gra-FI-a, with a soft g at the start. The plural is le geografie.
Stress the i: fo-to-gra-FI-a, not on the -to- as in English. It also means a photograph; short form: la foto.
Stress the i: bi-o-gra-FI-a. An autobiography is l'autobiografia (f.); plural le biografie.

lessons.title: -ry → -ria · Nouns in -ry
lessons.objective: -ry often becomes -ria: memory → memoria, theory → teoria.
lessons.explanation: Many -ry words differ: library → biblioteca, factory → fabbrica, grocery store → alimentari. history drops its h: storia, which also means story.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: It means both history and a story: la storia d'Italia, una bella storia. Say STO-ria, with the h of history dropped.
Stress the second syllable: me-MO-ria. It covers memory in the mind and in a computer.
Hold the tt: vit-TO-ria. The ct of victory becomes tt; the plural is le vittorie.

lessons.title: -or → -ore · Nouns in -or
lessons.objective: Add -e, and the noun is masculine: il colore, l'errore, il dottore.
lessons.explanation: People in -tore usually make the feminine with -trice: l'attore, l'attrice. dottore and professore take -essa: la dottoressa, la professoressa.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the tt: dot-TO-re. Feminine la dottoressa; dottore is also a polite title for any graduate.
Hold the tt: at-TO-re. Feminine l'attrice; plural gli attori.
Stress the -TO- syllable: mo-TO-re. The word covers an engine, so un motore a benzina is a gasoline engine.

lessons.title: -id → -ido · Adjectives in -id
lessons.objective: Add -o: rapid → rapido. The stress falls on the third syllable from the end, with no written accent: RA-pi-do.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each Italian word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the first syllable: RA-pi-do, with no written accent. Feminine rapida: una risposta rapida is a quick reply.
Stress the first syllable: LI-qui-do, with qu as kw. It is also a noun: il liquido, plural i liquidi.
Stress the first syllable: STU-pi-do. Feminine stupida, plural stupidi; it is as blunt as in English.

lessons.title: -ure → -ura · Nouns in -ure
lessons.objective: -ure becomes -ura, feminine: la cultura, la temperatura.
lessons.explanation: nature → natura works, but future → futuro and picture → quadro / foto are different.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second syllable: cul-TU-ra. The word is feminine, plural le culture.
Hold the tt and stress the -TU- syllable: let-te-ra-TU-ra. It also means the body of writing on a subject.
Stress -TU-: tem-pe-ra-TU-ra, five syllables. To take a temperature is misurare la temperatura; a fever is la febbre.

lessons.title: -an → -ano · Nationalities and -an words
lessons.objective: Add -o: American → americano, Mexican → messicano. Feminine is -ana.
lessons.explanation: Not every nationality: English → inglese, French → francese, German → tedesco. Italian writes nationalities with a small letter.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Note the double s: mes-si-CA-no, spelled with ss, not x. Feminine messicana.
Stress the -CA- syllable: a-me-ri-CA-no. Un caffè americano is an espresso topped up with hot water; plural americani.
Italian writes no h here: u-MA-no. Feminine umana; il genere umano is the human race.

lessons.title: -ion → -ione · Other -ion nouns
lessons.objective: Leftover -ion words add -e and are feminine: union → unione. (-tion and -sion have their own rules above.)
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each Italian word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the -NIO- syllable: u-NIO-ne, where ni runs together like ny. The plural is le unioni.
Stress the -NIO- syllable: o-pi-NIO-ne. In my opinion is secondo me; the plural is le opinioni.
Stress the middle: re-GIO-ne, with a soft g. It also names Italy's twenty administrative regions.

lessons.title: s + consonant → lo / uno · Initial s + consonant
lessons.objective: Italian words can begin with s + consonant, so nothing is added: station → stazione, space → spazio. Masculine nouns that start this way take lo and uno: lo spazio, uno stadio.
lessons.explanation: Only the spelling pattern is guaranteed: sport → lo sport, but speak → parlare. Feminine nouns keep la: la stazione.

items.note: Stress the -zio- syllable: sta-ZIO-ne; z sounds like ts. No extra vowel in front. Plural le stazioni.
No extra vowel in front: SPA-tsio. Masculine words starting s + consonant take lo, uno and plural gli.
Say STA-dio with no vowel before the st-. It takes lo, uno and plural gli stadi, because it starts with s + consonant.

lessons.title: ph → f · ph becomes f
lessons.objective: Italian never writes ph: every ph becomes f.

items.note: Stress the first syllable: FI-si-co, with a plain f. As a noun, il fisico also means a person's physique.
Short for la fotografia, so it stays feminine and does not change in the plural: le foto. Stress FO-to.
Stress the third syllable from the end: te-LE-fo-no. The plural is i telefoni.

lessons.title: th → t · th becomes t
lessons.objective: Italian has no th: it becomes t. theater → teatro.

items.note: Stress the a: te-A-tro, three syllables with a clear e then a. The t is a plain t, never English th.
Stress the -ri-: te-o-RI-a, four syllables. Plural le teorie.
Stress the -pi-: te-ra-PI-a. Plural le terapie.

lessons.title: x / bs / dv / pt → ss / ss / vv / tt · Clusters become double consonants
lessons.objective: Italian turns many consonant clusters into a double consonant: maximum → massimo, absolute → assoluto, adventure → avventura, adopt → adottare.
lessons.explanation: Hold every double consonant a beat longer: as-so-LU-to. x usually becomes ss: exact → esatto.

items.note: Hold the double v: av-ven-TU-ra. The English dv cluster becomes vv.
Hold the double s: MAS-si-mo, stressed on the first syllable. x becomes ss. Also an adjective: il voto massimo.
Hold the double s: as-so-LU-to. The feminine is assoluta; the plural is assoluti.

items.note: Hold the double z, a long dz sound, then stress -zio-: or-ga-niz-za-ZIO-ne. Plural le organizzazioni.
Stress the -zio- syllable: si-tua-ZIO-ne. Plural le situazioni.
In everyday use it means upbringing and good manners; schooling is l'istruzione. Stress e-du-ca-ZIO-ne.

Hold the double l: col-li-SIO-ne. The ll of collision stays double in Italian.
Stress the -sio- syllable: in-va-SIO-ne. The s sounds like z. Plural le invasioni.

lessons.objective: -ity becomes -ità, with a written accent on the final à. The noun is feminine: l'università, la comunità.

items.note: Generale drops its -e before -mente: ge-ne-ral-MEN-te. Stress the -MEN- syllable.
Hold the double m: im-me-dia-ta-MEN-te. It comes from the feminine immediata. In everyday speech, subito is more common.
Hold the double t: e-sat-ta-MEN-te. From esatta, the feminine of esatto. Also used alone as an answer: Esattamente!

lessons.title: -ble → -bile · Adjectives in -ble · 2
lessons.objective: -ible and -able become -ibile and -abile: possible → possibile, flexible → flessibile.
lessons.explanation: Double letters stay double, and the stress falls on the syllable before -bile: pos-SI-bi-le. comfortable is the exception: say comodo.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the double s and stress the syllable before -bile: fles-SI-bi-le. x becomes ss.
Stress the syllable before -bile: vi-SI-bi-le. The s sounds like z between vowels.
The -ible becomes -abile: re-spon-SA-bi-le. As a noun, il/la responsabile means the person in charge.

lessons.title: -ist → -ista · People and -ist words · 2
lessons.objective: Add -a: artist → artista. The singular is the same for men and women: il turista, la turista.
lessons.explanation: The plural shows the gender: i turisti for men or a mixed group, le turiste for women.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Hold the tt: ot-ti-MI-sta (pt becomes tt). One singular for men and women; plural gli ottimisti or le ottimiste.
Hold the double s: pes-si-MI-sta. Plural i pessimisti or le pessimiste.
Lo before s + consonant: lo specialista. Stress spe-cia-LI-sta; the c before i is soft, like ch in chair.

lessons.title: -ism → -ismo · Ideas and movements · 2
lessons.objective: Add -o: tourism → turismo. Masculine nouns: il turismo, l'ottimismo.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each Italian word and its spelling: optimism → ottimismo, racism → razzismo.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the -li-: ca-pi-ta-LI-smo. Masculine, and the plural is rarely used.
Only one m, unlike English: co-mu-NI-smo. Masculine: il comunismo.
Hold the double z, a long ts sound: raz-ZI-smo. The English c becomes zz.

lessons.title: -ic → -ico · Adjectives in -ic · 2
lessons.objective: -ic becomes -ico. The stress falls on the third syllable from the end, with no written accent: elettrico, fantastico, pubblico.
lessons.explanation: Nouns often end in -ica instead: music → musica, politics → politica. In the plural, -ico usually becomes -ici: elettrici, classici.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second syllable: ro-MAN-ti-co. The plural is romantici, with a soft c like ch in chair.
Stress e-co-NO-mi-co. It also means cheap: un ristorante economico.
Stress spe-CI-fi-co. The first c is soft (ch in chair), the last c is hard. Plural specifici.

lessons.title: -ical → -ico · Adjectives in -ical · 2
lessons.objective: -ical becomes -ico: practical → pratico, political → politico.
lessons.explanation: A few keep -ale: musicale, tropicale, verticale. medico is also the everyday word for a doctor: il medico.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress STO-ri-co. It comes from la storia, so the h of history disappears. Plural storici.
Stress LO-gi-co. The g before i is soft, like j in jam. Plural logici.
Stress TI-pi-co. The plural is tipici, with a soft c like ch in chair. Un piatto tipico is a local dish.

lessons.title: -al → -ale · Adjectives in -al · 2
lessons.objective: Add -e: normal → normale, final → finale, hospital → ospedale. Italian adds nothing in front of s + consonant: special → speciale.
lessons.explanation: attuale means current, not actual; actually is in realtà.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress ge-ne-RA-le. It is the same form for masculine and feminine. In general is in generale.
The h drops and the i becomes e: o-spe-DA-le. Masculine, plural gli ospedali.
Stress per-so-NA-le. Il personale also means the staff or personnel of a workplace.

lessons.title: -ive → -ivo · Adjectives in -ive · 2
lessons.objective: -ive becomes -ivo: active → attivo. Change the final vowel with the gender (attiva).
lessons.explanation: Watch the spelling: ct becomes tt (active → attivo). effettivo means actual or real; effective is efficace.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second-to-last syllable: ne-ga-TI-vo. The feminine is negativa, the plural negativi.
The x of exclusive becomes s: e-sclu-SI-vo. The feminine is esclusiva; the plural is esclusivi.
Hold the double cc, which sounds like tch before e, and the double ss: ec-ces-SI-vo.

lessons.title: -ous → -oso · Adjectives in -ous · 2
lessons.objective: -ous becomes -oso: famous → famoso. Feminine is -osa.
lessons.explanation: A few change completely: serious → serio, various → vari, dangerous → pericoloso.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the -RO-: ge-ne-RO-so. The g is soft, like j in jam. The feminine is generosa.
Stress ner-VO-so, not the first syllable. It often means irritable or on edge, not just anxious.
Stress the -RIO-: mi-ste-RIO-so. The feminine is misteriosa; the plural is misteriosi.

lessons.title: -ant / -ent → -ante / -ente · Adjectives and people in -ant / -ent · 2
lessons.objective: Add -e: important → importante, different → differente. Many also name people: lo studente, il presidente.
lessons.explanation: Double letters stay: different → differente. In everyday speech, diverso is the more common word for different.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Soft g before e: in-tel-li-GEN-te. Hold the double l. The form is the same for men and women.
Both an adjective and a noun: il paziente or la paziente is a patient in a clinic. Say pa-ZIEN-te, with z like ts.
The ending stays -e for both genders: il presidente, la presidente. Say pre-si-DEN-te, plural i presidenti.

lessons.title: -ence → -enza · Nouns in -ence · 2
lessons.objective: -ence becomes -enza, and the noun is feminine: la scienza, l'esperienza.
lessons.explanation: udienza is a hearing, but a crowd at a show is il pubblico. conferenza is a lecture or talk; a big meeting is un congresso.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Say sc before i or e like English sh: SCIEN-za. The plural is le scienze, as in scienze naturali.
Stress the second-to-last syllable: pre-SEN-za. The z sounds like ts. The adjective is presente.
Stress the second-to-last syllable: vio-LEN-za. The z sounds like ts, and the noun is feminine.

lessons.title: -ance → -anza · Nouns in -ance · 2
lessons.objective: -ance becomes -anza, feminine: l'importanza, la distanza.
lessons.explanation: A few -ance words take -enza instead: assistance → assistenza, resistance → resistenza.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second-to-last syllable: e-le-GAN-za. The g is hard here, as in go. The adjective is elegante.
The u becomes o and the b drops: so-STAN-za. In sostanza means basically, in essence.
Hold the double l: tol-le-RAN-za. The z sounds like ts. The verb is tollerare.

lessons.title: -ary → -ario · Nouns and adjectives in -ary · 2
lessons.objective: -ary becomes -ario: necessary → necessario, dictionary → dizionario.
lessons.explanation: library is a false friend: biblioteca. A libreria is a bookshop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: English c becomes g: se-gre-TA-rio. A woman is la segretaria. It is also the title of a party leader.
Usually a worker's wage. A monthly salary for an employee is lo stipendio. Say sa-LA-rio.
The z sounds like ts: di-zio-NA-rio, with stress on -NA-. It is masculine; the plural is i dizionari.

lessons.title: -ize → -izzare · Verbs in -ize · 2
lessons.objective: -ize becomes -izzare, with a double z: organize → organizzare. They conjugate like any -are verb.
lessons.explanation: realizzare means to carry out or achieve. To realize (understand) is rendersi conto.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: The double zz is a long dz sound: me-mo-riz-ZA-re. Conjugates like parlare: memorizzo, memorizzi.
Stress the -ZA-: mo-der-niz-ZA-re. Hold the double zz. The adjective is moderno.
Stress the -ZA-: le-ga-liz-ZA-re. Hold the double zz. It conjugates like parlare: legalizzo.

lessons.title: -ate → -are · Verbs in -ate · 2
lessons.objective: Replace -ate with -are: celebrate → celebrare, separate → separare.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each Italian word and its spelling: calculate → calcolare.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Say each vowel: cre-A-re, with stress on the A. The noun is la creazione. It conjugates like parlare: creo, crei.
It means to bring up, or to teach manners, more than to give schooling. The c is hard: e-du-CA-re.
Stress the -RA-: de-co-RA-re. It means to decorate a room or a cake, and also to award a medal.

lessons.title: -ify → -ificare · Verbs in -ify · 2
lessons.objective: -ify becomes -ificare: identify → identificare.
lessons.explanation: clarify is the one to watch: Italians say chiarire.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: The j of English becomes gi, said like j in jam: giu-sti-fi-CA-re. The c is hard: giustifico, giustifichi.
Hold the double s: clas-si-fi-CA-re. The c in -care stays hard, so it is classifico, classifichi.
Stress the -CA-: mo-di-fi-CA-re. The c is hard, so it is modifico but modifichi, with an h.

lessons.title: -ct → -tto · Words in -ct · 2
lessons.objective: ct becomes tt and the word adds -o: direct → diretto, perfect → perfetto.
lessons.explanation: The same change runs through fact → fatto, project → progetto, object → oggetto and subject → soggetto. A school subject is la materia.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second syllable: pro-DOT-to. Hold the double tt. Note the vowel: product → prodotto, with o, not u.
Hold the double tt: con-TAT-to. Mettersi in contatto con means to get in touch with.
Hold the double ff and the double tt: ef-FET-to. Italian says effetti speciali for special effects.

lessons.title: -ology → -logia · Fields of study · 2
lessons.objective: -ology becomes -logia, with the stress on the i: biology → biologia.
lessons.explanation: The noun is feminine and has no written accent: la biologia, la psicologia. Say bi-o-lo-GI-a.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Soft g twice: ge-o-lo-GI-a, stress on the i. The g in geo- sounds like j in jam.
Hard c, soft g: e-co-lo-GI-a, stress on the i. In everyday talk it also covers care for the environment.
The ci sounds like English ch: so-cio-lo-GI-a, with stress on the i. The ending -gia has a soft g.

lessons.title: -ologist → -ologo · Specialists in a field · 2
lessons.objective: -ologist becomes -ologo (feminine -ologa): biologist → biologo.
lessons.explanation: The stress falls on the third syllable from the end: bi-O-lo-go. The plural is -ologi: i biologi, gli psicologi.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress e-CO-lo-go; plural gli ecologi. This is the scientist: an environmental activist is un ambientalista.
Say so-CIO-lo-go, with ci sounding like ch. The feminine is la sociologa, the plural i sociologi.
Stress the third syllable from the end: ra-DIO-lo-go. The feminine is la radiologa, the plural i radiologi.

lessons.title: -graphy → -grafia · Writing and recording words · 2
lessons.objective: -graphy becomes -grafia, with the stress on the i: photography → fotografia.
lessons.explanation: ph becomes f and the noun is feminine: la geografia. In speech, la foto is the short form of la fotografia.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the i: co-re-o-gra-FI-a. The ch of English becomes c, and the ph becomes f.
Hold the double l: cal-li-gra-FI-a. It also means handwriting: una bella calligrafia.
Stress the i: bi-blio-gra-FI-a. The ph becomes f, and the noun is feminine.

lessons.title: -ry → -ria · Nouns in -ry · 2
lessons.objective: -ry often becomes -ria: memory → memoria, theory → teoria.
lessons.explanation: Many -ry words differ: library → biblioteca, factory → fabbrica, grocery store → alimentari. history drops its h: storia, which also means story.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the first syllable: GLO-ria. Here gl is a plain g + l, as in English glory.
Stress the second syllable: in-DU-stria. It means the sector or a manufacturing business. The noun is feminine.
Hard c and hard g: ca-te-go-RI-a, with stress on the i. It is feminine and the plural is le categorie.

lessons.title: -or → -ore · Nouns in -or · 2
lessons.objective: Add -e, and the noun is masculine: il colore, l'errore, il dottore.
lessons.explanation: People in -tore usually make the feminine with -trice: l'attore, l'attrice. dottore and professore take -essa: la dottoressa, la professoressa.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each Italian word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Stress the second syllable: co-LO-re. The plural is i colori. Di che colore? means what color?
Hold the double r: er-RO-re. It is masculine, so l'errore, with plural gli errori.
Hold the double s: pro-fes-SO-re. The feminine is la professoressa. It means a teacher in secondary school too.
